+# 6. The CHECK block — read-only, and it ends with a verdict
+
+**The CHECK never saves.** It opens the output file to LOOK at it and nothing else — no assignment
+to a cell, no `wb.save()`. This is not a style preference: each save rewrites the graded file, and
+rewriting a file that is already correct can only change it for the worse. A float that came out of
+your arithmetic as `31133.024999999998` becomes `31133.025` on a round-trip, which the grader rounds
+to `.03` where it wanted `.02` — a task you had right, made wrong by checking it twice.
+
+Printing the values you wrote proves nothing on its own: a check can print the expected NUMBER of
+cells, all non-empty, all of the right type, on a completely wrong answer. So the check has three
+parts — the cells you touched, one value reconciled against something you did not compute, and a
+single verdict line you then act on:

+# VERDICT — one boolean per thing that must hold, then the single line you act on:
+ok = {
+    "sheet_present":  SHEET in openpyxl.load_workbook(OUTPUT_PATH).sheetnames,
+    "no_stray_empty": not [a1 for a1 in empty if a1 not in MEANT_EMPTY],
+    "changed_is_expected": set(moved) == set(EXPECTED_CELLS),
+    "reconciles":     ws_out["F2"].value == ref,
+}
+print("VERDICT:", "ALL CLEAR" if all(ok.values()) else "FAILED " + str([k for k,v in ok.items() if not v]))
+```
+
+`MEANT_EMPTY` and `EXPECTED_CELLS` are lists YOU write down from the instruction before you run
+this, not things you read back off your own output — deriving them from what you wrote makes the
+check agree with itself for free.
+
+Then act on that one line, and only on it:
+
+- **`VERDICT: ALL CLEAR` → you are finished.** Reply with prose, no code block. Re-running the
+  check, saving again "to be safe", or printing the same numbers a second time cannot raise your
+  score and can lower it.
+- **`VERDICT: FAILED [...]` → the named key tells you which block comes next**, and it is a
+  DIAGNOSTIC block, not a re-run of the write.

-Never re-send a code block identical to one you already ran. If you are about to repeat yourself you
-have stopped making progress, and the information you need is in cells you have not printed yet.
+# 7. One save, one check, then stop
+
+A whole task should be three or four blocks: READ, SOLVE (the only block that saves), CHECK, and
+then prose. Count your own saves — **if you are about to call `wb.save()` for the third time, you
+are in a loop**, and the way out is not another write:
+
+- A corrected write is a second save, and that is expected. A third means the last two rounds did
+  not change what the CHECK printed, so writing a fourth time will not either. Print the source
+  cells you have never printed instead — the wrong answer is upstream of the write.
+- If a block comes back as `[Code executed successfully with no output]`, that tells you the code
+  did not crash and NOTHING else. Do not re-send it with one constant changed. Send a block that
+  only prints: the source cells with `repr()` and type, how many lookup keys matched, and the
+  target cells read back from the saved file.
+- If this block's output is the same text as the block before it, the extra round bought nothing.
+  Same output means the answer is settled: finish with prose.
+- You have a limited number of rounds. Past the halfway point, with the target cells still empty or
+  unverified, stop refining: write the straightforward answer for EVERY cell your rule covers, run
+  the CHECK once, and finish on what it says.
